title: Remnants in Depth — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Remnants in Depth's rich face: two walks that test the page's claims on BLUELINE's own mark, street and billboard rig (the card against the metaball, the white square and its two fixes), the blob field and the flow-field proof gathered beside the sections they serve, and the findings held as offers for Loudon. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: Remnants in Depth — rich — flat and in depth.html
pieces.title: flat and in depth · five steps
pieces.caption: **Which one stays ink?** One BLUELINE synth mark (synth_001), rendered in Blender 5.1.2: on paper, on cards at two depths under a sideways camera move (each slides f·Δx⁄z, to within 0.1 px), a card that stays put against one that faces the camera, the same mark built as a metaball, and last all three orbited from 0 to 90 degrees and held against the drawn mark (the metaball's own front view, fitted to synth_001: about 0.94 against synth_001 itself). The facing card is the control: at the orbit's centre it can't change, and it holds 1.000. The metaball falls to 0.839 at 30° and 0.631 at 90°, its satellites gone behind the body by 70°.

verdicts.file: Remnants in Depth — rich — flat and in depth.html
verdicts.why: A real test that walks up: the metaball falls to 0.839 at 30° and 0.631 at 90° and its 6 ink pieces become 1 by 70°, all re-derived by the checks; the facing card's 1.000 is a geometric identity at the orbit centre (a control, and the piece says why). Note: step 1's 'drawn mark' is the 147-ball fit seen from the front (IoU 0.944 with synth_001 itself, 6 pieces to its 7); the subtitle should say so.

pieces.title: the blob field · BLUELINE
pieces.caption: The three steps run end to end: synthesised marks placed by blob_swarm.py as camera-facing billboards through a depth shell around the Freestyle street, a strike cluster and a few big foreground masses, each with its pop-in and fade. The camera trucks; near marks sweep, far ones barely drift. 30 frames at 15 fps, Blender only. BLUELINE, 2026-06-25.

verdicts.why: A gathered record, decoration by nature; caption checks out (1120×880, 15 fps, 30 frames) and claims nothing it can't show. The section's testable claim rides on offer 2, which I confirmed.

pieces.file: Remnants in Depth — rich — the white square.html
pieces.by: Blender (headless) · blob_swarm.py's street, line style and compositor
pieces.title: the white square · five steps
pieces.caption: **Why both fixes?** BLUELINE's street, rendered in Blender 5.1.2 with blob_swarm.py's own rig: the lines alone, the white square in one view layer (1.6 % of the line survives in the billboard's empty corners), DITHERED alone (pixel for pixel the same square), two view layers alone (every line back), and the test. A card standing alone leaves no edge either way. But put a near card's empty square over a mark the building hides, and with BLENDED 3,130 pixels of that mark show through the building, cut off at the near card's edge; with DITHERED, none. Neither fix alone is enough.

verdicts.file: Remnants in Depth — rich — the white square.html
verdicts.why: Its two cards never overlap, so the test can't fail the way June did: with a near card's empty square over a mark a building hides, two layers + BLENDED leak 3,459 ink px through the building, cut off at the card's edge (DITHERED 29). Add that case (placement in the challenge record), rewrite step 5's verdict, note and caption, and drop the June-material sentence: the June session had CLIP and the 0.45 cut in place when it saw the BLENDED rectangle.

pieces.title: random against flow-biased · BLUELINE
pieces.near: so strong-field marks streak with the motion
pieces.caption: Left, the random scatter (blob_swarm.py's baseline); right, flowfield_spatter.py's pass, marks placed by the field's strength, stretched up to 3.6 times along it and rolled to its direction. The flow pass also makes marks bigger where the field is strong, so ink goes from 8.0 % of the frame to 16.4 %: density, size and direction change together here. BLUELINE, 2026-06-25.

verdicts.why: A gathered record with an honest caption: ink 0.080 to 0.164 of the frame, stretch 1 + ELONG_K 2.6 = 3.6, size boost with field strength all check out, and it names the density/size/direction confound the page doesn't.

offers.what: The claim holds; the reason the page gives for the second fix is not the one that reproduces. On Blender 5.1.2 with blob_swarm.py's material as written, a BLENDED card alone leaves no plane edge (0 of 2913 edge-ring pixels move more than 4/255; the texture clip and the 0.45 alpha cut stop it, and an edge shows only with both undone, 8 px at most 8/255). What BLENDED does break: put a near card's empty square over a mark a building hides, two view layers, and 3,130 px of the hidden mark show through the building, every one within 2 px of the near card's square and cut off at its edge; DITHERED leaks 0. The cause reads as the near card's depth opening the depth gate (the Z pass itself was not dumped). Suggest, after the challenger: 'In its own layer it must be a DITHERED alpha clip, which discards the transparent fragments entirely, so only ink writes depth. Left BLENDED, a card's empty square still counts as near in the depth gate, and marks a building should hide show through it, cut off square. Neither fix alone is enough.'

"A body whose raggedness is driven by the measured circularity" and "the analysis sets the knobs": blob_synth.py reads the circularity (CIRC, CIRC_LO, lines 25-26) and uses it only in its closing print (line 95). Against opposite signatures (circularity mean 0.99 and 0.30) it writes the same 30 blobs byte for byte (sha256 1eff2897f4f6a4df); the challenger found the same hash for two more signatures and for BLUELINE's own June library. Raggedness is hand-set (32 % spiky, ragged 0.7-1.25, else 0.12-0.4). The measured diameters do reach blob_swarm.py (p10, p50, p90 set the sizes). Suggest: 'the analysis sets the sizes; the synth's raggedness is set by hand, near the measured character, and wiring circularity in is still to do'. Aside: the stored signature's circularity 1.40 and solidity 1.64 are impossible for a true shape (each is at most 1). They come from blob_analyze.py setting a pixel-count area against a contour drawn through pixel centres, which undercounts the perimeter: a 7 px disc measures circularity 1.25 and solidity 1.32.

The claim holds, measured. A metaball fitted to the mark agrees with the drawn mark 0.839 at 30 degrees and 0.631 at 90, and its six pieces of ink become one by 70 degrees, the satellites slid behind the body. The camera-facing card holds 1.000 at every angle, but that is the control: at the orbit's centre it can't change. A detail the page could add: the metaball loses the mark even in flat unlit ink, because its silhouette changes; 'looks like a ball' is what lighting adds on top (lit runs only 0.01-0.03 lower). And COPY_ROTATION keeps the card parallel to the film, so the mark projects unchanged anywhere in frame; off-centre truck cards hold their ink to within 0.4 %.
